Amaryllidaceae.key_door: bulb + scape + spathe-bracted umbel + 6 tepals + 6 stamens; route by ovary position and alliaceous odor

Iridaceae.key_door: equitant/2-ranked leaves + 6 tepals + 3 stamens + inferior ovary + capsule

anchor_families.Orchidaceae: inferior ovary comparison; labellum + column + usually one fertile stamen

lineage_lesson: Asparagales repeatedly uses 3+3 tepals. The most useful project-level splits are stamen number, ovary position, inflorescence architecture, and specialized floral structures rather than 'straplike leaves.'
taxonomy_notes: Allium canadense L., Allium drummondii, Nothoscordum bivalve, Zephyranthes drummondii and Zephyranthes chlorosolen are accepted current species under Kew.
Cooperia drummondii is retained only as provenance for accepted Zephyranthes chlorosolen.
Nemastylis geminiflora is accepted; Nemastylis texana and Calydorea texana are historical synonym concepts.
Sisyrinchium angustifolium, S. ensigerum, S. biforme and S. langloisii remain current accepted project concepts.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Ovary position is not universal across project Amaryllidaceae: superior in Allium/Nothoscordum, inferior in Zephyranthes.
Do not identify Iridaceae from grasslike or swordlike leaves alone; require the 3-stamen/inferior-ovary reproductive package.
